Three-dimensional mid-domain null model for marine and other volumes

geo_mde_3d.Rd

geo_mde_3d() extends geo_mde() to volumes: the sea, lakes, caves or a forest canopy, where species occupy a range in depth as well as on the map. The domain is the water column defined by a bathymetry raster, divided into depth bands; a band exists in a cell if the sea floor there is deeper than the top of the band. Each species keeps its observed range size in grid cells x depth bands (voxels) and is placed at random nsim times with the spreading-dye algorithm, growing into the six face-neighbouring voxels (north, south, east, west, up and down), so ranges stay contiguous and follow the coastline and the sea floor.

A species' observed range (range = "hull") is the convex hull of its records on the map, in every depth band between its shallowest and deepest record (range-through interpolation in depth), restricted to the domain; range = "cells" uses the occupied voxels only. With one depth band the model equals geo_mde(); on a single water column it equals the one-dimensional model along depth.

Usage

geo_mde_3d(
  data,
  bathymetry,
  breaks,
  depth = depth,
  species = species,
  range = c("hull", "buffer", "cells"),
  buffer = NULL,
  nsim = 199,
  conf = 0.95,
  lon = lon,
  lat = lat
)

Arguments

data

Occurrence records with a depth column: an sf object of points or a data frame with longitude and latitude.

bathymetry

A SpatRaster of sea-floor depth in metres, positive downwards (cells that are land or NA are outside the domain). Its grid is the grid of the model.

breaks

Depth band limits in metres, increasing from 0.

depth

Column with the depth of each record (metres, positive).

species

Column with species names.

range

How each species' range is built from its records: "hull" (the convex hull), "buffer" (all cells within buffer metres of a record) or "cells" (occupied cells only). Hulls suit continuous ranges on land; buffers suit species tied to patchy habitat such as reefs, coasts or mountain tops, where a hull would span unsuitable ground between distant records.

buffer

Buffer distance in metres for range = "buffer"; by default twice the cell size.

nsim

Number of randomisations.

conf

Width of the simulation interval.

lon, lat

Coordinate columns when data is not sf.

Value

A list with observed, expected, sd, lower, upper and ses, each a SpatRaster with one layer per depth band; profile, a tibble with the mean observed and expected richness per water voxel, and its interval, for every depth band (the vertical richness profile); and fit, as in geo_mde().

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  bathy <- terra::rast(nrows = 10, ncols = 10, xmin = 0, xmax = 10, ymin = 0, ymax = 10,
    crs = "EPSG:3857", vals = rep(seq(10, 300, length.out = 10), 10))
  set.seed(1)
  recs <- data.frame(x = runif(200, 0, 10), y = runif(200, 0, 10),
    depth = runif(200, 0, 250), species = sample(letters, 200, TRUE))
  recs <- sf::st_as_sf(recs, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3857)
  m <- geo_mde_3d(recs, bathy, breaks = c(0, 50, 100, 200, 300), nsim = 19)
  m$profile
}
#> # A tibble: 4 × 8
#>   band        top bottom n_voxels observed expected lower upper
#>   <fct>     <dbl>  <dbl>    <int>    <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 0-50 m        0     50      100     8.01     7.88  4.69  11.4
#> 2 50-100 m     50    100       80     9.71     9.61  6.29  13.2
#> 3 100-200 m   100    200       70    10.7      9.65  6.17  13.1
#> 4 200-300 m   200    300       40     6.42     8.75  5.51  12.3
# }
